subject: Before Nine in the Morning
fact: Bookwyrm’s whereabouts before nine in the morning are unverified and critical to establishing her alibi — this temporal anchor is a key point of investigation.
source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning.

subject: Day I Was Sleeping
fact: The day the player missed the silent communication lesson is one among many days they were sleeping — a recurring pattern that symbolizes avoidance, distraction, or disengagement from deeper truths. Glabbagool’s mastery contrasts sharply with this neglect.
source_quote: There are, by now, a great many days I was sleeping. 'Was I ever there?'

subject: day of the murder
fact: The murder occurred on a specific day referenced by Grygum’s timeline — including events from eight o’clock onward, and the morning inspection.
source_quote: The morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight...

subject: death time
fact: The victim died at precisely midnight.
source_quote: He died at roughly midnight

subject: December 31st, 1999
fact: December 31st, 1999, referenced as the release date of the film *End of Days*, serves as a cultural touchstone for the investigator’s analogy regarding the ambiguity of 'midnight' in magical contexts.
source_quote: Did you ever see, the Schwarzenegger movie End of Days that came out in 1999?

subject: eight o'clock
fact: Eight o’clock is a critical temporal anchor — marking Grygum’s meeting with Janussi and the initial inspection on the day of the murder.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting... the inspection just after eight.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: Midnight of Death
fact: The victim died at midnight — a precise temporal anchor that became the critical clue linking the poison’s delayed effect to the timing of the murder.
source_quote: He died at roughly midnight.

subject: midnight of the murder
fact: The murder occurred precisely at midnight, matching the delayed effect of midnight tears poison, and is the temporal anchor for all forensic reconstruction.
source_quote: The creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight. He died at roughly midnight.

subject: night of the murder
fact: The murder occurred on the night of the event, with Janussi consuming the poison during the day and dying precisely at midnight; the impersonation of Sylvira Savikas occurred that same night; Kalan’s last verified sighting of Janussi was at the eight o’clock meeting, and his body was discovered shortly after midnight.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'The morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher.'

subject: poisoning time
fact: The poison was transferred by licking a finger and turning pages, implicating the book.
source_quote: the poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages

subject: quarter-past-ten
fact: Quarter-past-ten is the time Grygum claims to have met Sylvira Savikas — later revealed to be a deception.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas...

subject: quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas
fact: Kalan claimed to have visited Sylvira Savikas at quarter-past-ten on the night of the murder, but this alibi was compromised by the revelation that Sylvira had been impersonated; this time stamp is now a critical point of investigation, as the real Sylvira may have been elsewhere, or the impersonator was active during this window.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.'

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during the investigation phase following the Candlekeep Murders, after the dispersal of the Council of the Great Readers and before the final episode of the investigators' work.
source_quote: we're down to the last episode, and we're saving it.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 11th hour of the day, Janussi the philistine’s meeting.
source_quote: The eleven o'clock meeting came out without resistance — Janussi the *philistine*

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: time of Fheminor’s beating (around 8 AM)
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark was beaten around 8 AM — hours before the murder. This timing suggests he may have witnessed something or been silenced before the killing, making him a potential key witness or victim of a cover-up.
source_quote: find out when the man got beaten up, because beat-up-at-eight tells a different story than beat-up-when-he-died.

subject: time of murder (before 9 AM)
fact: The murder occurred before 9 AM, and Bookwyrm’s whereabouts during that window are unknown. Establishing her alibi is critical to determining her involvement. The timeline of the victim’s last known movements and the timing of the impersonation are key to the investigation.
source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning... available to be a suspect.

subject: time of Sylvira’s impersonation (night of the murder)
fact: The impersonation of Sylvira Savikas occurred during the night of the murder, as she was seen walking the halls with a lantern. This timing links the impersonator directly to the crime scene and suggests premeditation and intimate knowledge of the library’s routines.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: assignment of Deneir's Sanctum as office
fact: Bookwyrm assigned Deneir's Sanctum as the investigators' operational base, offering staff support and access to the library. The generosity of this gesture is viewed with suspicion — the room may be bugged, and the staff may be surveillance assets, turning the office into a controlled environment.
source_quote: It's nice and all to offer up that we can use the office, and that they'll go fetch people, and all of those sorts of things, but it's also a little suspect.

subject: Bonding of Glabbagool and Zalthir
fact: Glabbagool chose Zalthir as his host, not through force or ritual, but by slipping onto his arm and declaring their union — a moment that revealed Zalthir’s failure to understand silent communication.
source_quote: And he flowed up onto my arm. Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: book poisoning method
fact: The victim was poisoned by ingesting midnight tears dust that had been applied to pages he licked while reading.
source_quote: Some liquid had gotten onto his finger, and the finger had gone black. [...] The dust reacts on contact with spit, and a man turning pages licks his fingers to do it.

subject: book reading contradiction
fact: Daral gave Janussi a book to teach its worth, then was enraged when Janussi read it.
source_quote: you gave him a book, you were furious to find him reading it

subject: bookwyrm's dismissal
fact: Bookwyrm officially dismissed Kalan from the case, but he remains involved unofficially, creating internal conflict.
source_quote: Bookwyrm had made it official that he was to be nowhere near it. "Officially," I said. "See, there you go."

subject: collaboration proposal between the party and Kalan
fact: Kalan proposes an offline, private sync-up with the party to merge all findings into one unified analysis, acknowledging their superior progress and agreeing to work together despite his official exclusion.
source_quote: He proposed it in the most extraordinary terms — offline chat, private work streams, a meeting to examine everything one by one, the four of us and him, five streams, merge it all in a few hours. 'I hope you actually used the word sync up,' I said. 'That makes me happy.'

subject: Corrosive Embrace Demonstration
fact: Glabbagool demonstrated his corrosive embrace on a restrained target, revealing it does not wound but dissolves — leaving nothing behind. This ability requires a prior binding and exacts a cost from him, marking it as both powerful and perilous.
source_quote: It was not a wound. It was dissolution. A target restrained, nothing left to hold by the end of it.

subject: Council Meeting After Murder
fact: The council convened after a murder with competing demands: leadership change, succession naming, dismissal of the gate warden, and urgent calls to find the murderer — revealing fractured authority and conflicting priorities.
source_quote: A'lai Aivenmore wanting a vote and new leadership... Kazryn Nyantani cutting through with first you must find the murderer.

subject: Daral's finger-flicking
fact: Daral wet his finger and began flicking through the pages, reading himself a funny passage until he was laughing again.
source_quote: He wet his finger and began flicking through the pages, reading himself a funny passage until he was laughing again.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz asked aloud who they were working for, and Grygum answered 'Justice.'
source_quote: Who are we working for, exactly?" "Justice," said Grygum.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz corrected Daral’s mocking label of them as 'Bookwyrm's brownnosers.'
source_quote: That's not our," Grygum said, "that's not our chosen name.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz gave Bookwyrm the harmless witness Ms. Hollypocket to chew on.
source_quote: I gave her one harmless witness to chew on, Ms. Hollypocket, whom we'd already seen anyway.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Bookwyrm introduced the half-elf as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma.
source_quote: Bookwyrm waved them off and ushered us in herself, all warmth, and introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Bookwyrm offered Deneir's Sanctum as their office and assigned Fembris to fetch witnesses and Vooshadi to stand the door.
source_quote: Then she took us to a nearby room, Deneir's Sanctum, a little shrine and library given over to the art of writing, and offered it up as our office. Fembris would fetch any witness we named. Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Daral Yashenti set the venue for the interrogation — the Hearth — making the investigators walk to him.
source_quote: Daral was not coming to us. We were to go to the Hearth.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed Bookwyrm dismissing Kei with the instruction to take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.
source_quote: *yes, Kei, you can take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that Bookwyrm insisted they not move through Candlekeep without one of them.
source_quote: one more thing, lightly placed: we shouldn't move through Candlekeep without one of them.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that Daral Yashenti was boisterous, flushed, and conspicuously delighted with his own existence.
source_quote: Boisterous, flushed, conspicuously delighted with his own existence.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz questioned whether the room was bugged or if their work would be private.
source_quote: Do we think the room is, like, bugged," I asked the others once we had a moment, "or has, like, secret — like, the stuff we do in there is actually going to be private to us, or do we need —

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recalled that the adjutant had attached himself to them the way an acolyte attaches to anyone who might be doing something more interesting than copying manuscripts.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer practically vibrated. The adjutant had attached himself to us the way an acolyte attaches to anyone who might be doing something more interesting than copying manuscripts

subject: Daz
fact: Daz reported to Bookwyrm that they had given generalities about talking to people and forming opinions on suspects.
source_quote: Generalities," I said. "That we went and talked to all the people that we could talk to. And we're forming an opinion on what may have happened, and who — like, we have a couple suspects that we would like to pursue, due to perceiving that they may have a motivation, or that other people have pointed them out.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz sorted Bookwyrm into the column marked *not above suspicion*.
source_quote: I sorted her into the column marked *not above suspicion* and kept walking.

subject: Discovery of Altered Notes
fact: The investigators discovered that their own notes contained an entry for 'Fheminor Scrivenbark' without a name — indicating internal corruption or magical interference in their records.
source_quote: It isn't… for some reason, there's no name on that entry. It just says, Fheminor Scrivenbark.

subject: discovery of Sylvira Savikas impersonation
fact: It is revealed that someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas on the night of the murder, a fact unknown to Kalan, which shifts suspicion toward a broader conspiracy involving deception and identity manipulation.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder? He went still. 'No. That is new information.'

subject: discovery of the sapphire summoning spell
fact: The sapphire associated with the High Tower key is not for freezing or protecting the key, but for a summoning spell that recalls the key to the holder’s hand from anywhere, rendering physical concealment unnecessary; this means the key could have been hidden in a river, a vault, or another plane and retrieved at will, eliminating the need for a physical key on the body.
source_quote: Grygum said: 'You don't hide the key on a body where someone can search it. You hide it nowhere at all, and you summon it when the door is in front of you.'

subject: eight o'clock meeting with Janussi
fact: Grygum met with Janussi at eight o’clock to request more watchers and was refused — a key point in his alibi and timeline.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused.

subject: false Sylvira impersonation
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas on the night of the murder, a deception unknown to Kalan until revealed.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder? [...] That is new information.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool went still for more than a minute when asked about the art of movement.
source_quote: Glabbagool went still. Not paused. Still. The difference matters. Paused costs something; still costs nothing. The better part of a minute passed.

subject: Glabbagool's answer to the monk
fact: Glabbagool answered, 'The body that mimics nothing is already shaped by what it watches.'
source_quote: Glabbagool went still. Then he answered. 'The body that mimics nothing is already shaped by what it watches.'

subject: Glabbagool's corrosive embrace
fact: Glabbagool's corrosive embrace dissolves a target restrained — nothing left to hold by the end of it.
source_quote: It was not a wound. It was dissolution. A target restrained, nothing left to hold by the end of it.

subject: Glabbagool's stillness
fact: Glabbagool answered the question of movement by going perfectly still, embodying wisdom.
source_quote: Glabbagool went still. Not paused. Still. The difference matters.

subject: Glabbagool's stillness
fact: Glabbagool went still — not paused, but still — for the better part of a minute, holding the silence as if it were the easiest thing he had ever been asked to do.
source_quote: Glabbagool went still. Not paused. Still. The difference matters. Paused costs something; still costs nothing. The better part of a minute passed.

subject: Glabbagool's summons
fact: Glabbagool was called before the Whispering Dome for judgment, and the narrator followed without question — a ritual of absolute attachment.
source_quote: I had no objection to log. He moseyed across the floor toward the Dome... and I followed. Of course I followed. That was never a question I was going to be asked twice.

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool chose to attach to Zalthir not for power, but for housekeeping — checking on the drow first.
source_quote: his instinct, at the moment of his own transformation, was housekeeping.

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool flowed up onto Zalthir's arm and settled along it like he had measured it in advance.
source_quote: And he flowed up onto my arm. Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool underwent a transformation during which he mastered the lesson of stillness in under a minute, demonstrating profound understanding of the Shadow Monk teachings. He emerged with new abilities tied to darkness, binding, and dissolution, and immediately reoriented himself onto the player’s arm.
source_quote: Glabbagool went still. Not paused. Still. The difference matters. Paused costs something; still costs nothing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum concluded the murder weapon was a book doped with midnight tears, which Janussi read himself to death.
source_quote: The book was the murder weapon, and he'd read himself dead.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum confirmed that midnight tears darken upon contact with saliva, explaining the blackened fingers and lips.
source_quote: The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva. The ochre reacts on contact with spit, and a man turning pages licks his fingers to do it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum discovered that midnight tears — a toxic pale ochre dust from the Feywild — becomes lethal only when ingested and activates at midnight.
source_quote: Midnight tears. A highly toxic pale ochre dust, made from the pollen of a plant usually found only in the Feywild. The creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum identified the sapphire spell as a summoning working that retrieves a hidden object into the caster’s hand.
source_quote: It's an old summoning working — the kind that calls a single hidden thing back into your hand.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed that their notes listed Fheminor Scrivenbark with no name on the entry.
source_quote: It isn't… for some reason, there's no name on that entry. It just says, Fheminor Scrivenbark.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum questioned whether summarizing the events was the same as finding out who did it.
source_quote: True? I thought we were asked to find out what — well, I guess summarizing the events is pretty much the same as finding out who did it from one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the sapphire summoning spell cannot be used on objects worn as jewelry, because 'carried' does not include 'worn.'
source_quote: It doesn't, as it turned out. Which reframed the whole use. 'Oh, I see,' I said, 'so you can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, "It doesn't seem just friendly."
source_quote: It doesn't seem just friendly," Grygum said.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suggested starting together and branching later to cover poison and Sylvira at once.
source_quote: Grygum wanted to start together and branch later. The reasoning was simple enough: split, and we cover the poison and Sylvira at once, but each of us walks into his own conversation alone, no second pair of hands to steady the work.

subject: Grygum's timeline reconstruction
fact: Grygum reconstructed his movements on the day of the murder to establish an alibi — including meetings, visits, and inspections.
source_quote: He gave us his timeline — the eight o'clock meeting... the quarter-past-ten visit... the return to the Chamber...

subject: impersonation of Sylvira Savikas
fact: An unknown individual impersonated Sylvira Savikas, wearing her face and carrying a lantern through Candlekeep’s halls at night. This act suggests deep knowledge of the library’s layout and personnel, and possibly a connection to forbidden texts or rituals. Bookwyrm’s subtle steering of the investigation toward Sylvira implies personal stakes.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: impersonation of Sylvira Savikas
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas on the night of the murder — a revelation that contradicted Grygum’s timeline and exposed a critical blind spot.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?

subject: inspection after eight on day of murder
fact: Grygum conducted an inspection just after eight on the day of the murder, followed by cordon, posted watcher, and doubled guard at the High Tower Library.
source_quote: The morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher, the state of emergency, the doubled guard.

subject: Janussi sitting upon Daral
fact: Janussi sat upon Daral like a common thug, in self-defense.
source_quote: Janussi had sat upon him like a common thug

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan acknowledged the possibility of shapeshifters and warned the investigators to watch their backs.
source_quote: I'm just saying," I said, and let him go to his research.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan confirmed he could question the dead and pull hidden truths into view if necessary.
source_quote: Yes — if such a thing should become necessary. So if we suspected someone was lying, he could sort it out? 'Of course I could.'

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan confirmed his return to the Chamber of Lost Lore for private research.
source_quote: The return to the Chamber of Lost Lore for private research.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan confirmed his visit to Sylvira Savikas at quarter-past-ten for a cosmological question.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan confirmed the High Tower is watched at all times, regardless of whether the key is in someone's pocket.
source_quote: The tower is watched. Always. People stand at it whether the key is in someone's pocket or not.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan confirmed the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher, and the doubled guard at the High Tower Library on the morning of the murder.
source_quote: The morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher, the state of emergency, the doubled guard at the High Tower Library.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan noticed the heart was hacked out after death to spoil resurrection.
source_quote: Yeah, we got that.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan noticed the poison in the left hand and the saliva on the victim’s fingers.
source_quote: The black stuff, yes, we saw that.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan offered to meet offline, in private work streams, to examine everything one by one with the five of them.
source_quote: He proposed it in the most extraordinary terms — offline chat, private work streams, a meeting to examine everything one by one, the four of us and him, five streams, merge it all in a few hours.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan pressed a small brass key into the cleric's palm and chose the orc, believing it was not chance.
source_quote: Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked, swept the corridor left, then right, and pressed a small brass key specifically into the cleric's palm.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan reconsidered his assumption that the murderer was the same person who rifled the safe after being challenged.
source_quote: I don't know. What I thought — but now that you bring it up, perhaps I was a little bit too hasty. Perhaps it was two different people.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan refused to be found at his post if he were killed, implying he expected to be targeted.
source_quote: If I and I do not see you tomorrow, do not look for me at my post.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan revealed he had been refused more watchers at the eight o'clock meeting.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan was unaware that someone had been pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder.
source_quote: No. That is new information.

subject: kalan's alibi timeline
fact: Kalan provided a detailed timeline: 8:00 meeting with Janussi, 10:15 visit to Sylvira, morning inspection, cordon, and doubled guard at the High Tower Library.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused, the quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas... the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher...

subject: Kalan's removal from the case
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was officially removed from the investigation by Bookwyrm, forcing him to operate unofficially, and he suspects the setup was designed to ensure outsiders like the party would bungle the case or remain silent.
source_quote: Bookwyrm had made it official that he was to be nowhere near it. 'Officially,' I said. 'See, there you go.' I believe you're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case, or else be silent if you do happen upon the right scent. You don't matter. You're outsiders.

subject: murder investigation
fact: The murder investigation involved conflicting assumptions about the safe, the locket, and the identity of the killer — later revised after new evidence emerged.
source_quote: Two hands had searched that apartment — one that knew exactly where to look, one that didn't.

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi was murdered by ingestion of midnight tears, administered via a book he licked his fingers to turn, dying precisely at midnight, with his fingers and lips blackened by the poison’s reaction to saliva, and his heart removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection.
source_quote: The black stuff, yes, we saw that. Yeah, we got that. The heart hacked out — after death, to spoil resurrection. The book was the murder weapon, and he'd read himself dead. He died at roughly midnight.

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi was murdered with 'midnight tears,' a Feywild poison ingested during the day that activates at midnight; his fingers and lips were blackened by saliva reacting with the poison, indicating he licked pages of a contaminated book; his heart was removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection; the second High Tower key, once carried in his locket, was stolen along with the locket itself.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'The heart hacked out — after death, to spoil resurrection.'

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi, a senior scholar and keeper of Candlekeep’s high towers, was murdered by poison. His body showed signs of prior trauma and was found in a locked chamber. His death triggered the investigation and exposed fractures in the library’s leadership and security.
source_quote: The body went to be purified... 'Zalthir made sure of that' — poison off his fingers and his lip too.

subject: poisoning of Janussi
fact: Janussi was poisoned by a substance transferred through a book he licked while turning its pages, implicating the person who handled the book with wet fingers.
source_quote: The poison was carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: Poisoning of Janussi
fact: Janussi was poisoned through a book he licked while turning its pages — a method that implicates only someone who handled the book with direct oral contact.
source_quote: The dead poisoner is the innocent one. A man does not lace the pages he's been licking all night.

subject: quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas
fact: Grygum visited Sylvira Savikas at quarter-past-ten to discuss a cosmological question — later revealed to have been an impersonation.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.

subject: secret key transfer
fact: Kalan Strongbranch secretly transferred the second High Tower key to Grygum during a concealed meeting, bypassing all other investigators. He did so because he fears he will be killed for it, and wants the key preserved outside his control.
source_quote: I have given it now to someone who is not me. If I and I do not see you tomorrow, do not look for me at my post.

subject: shapeshifter impersonation of Sylvira Savikas
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder, a deception unknown to Kalan until Zalthir revealed it; this suggests the killer or their accomplice has access to high-level illusion or transformation magic and may be attempting to misdirect the investigation.
source_quote: Zalthir said: 'Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?'

subject: silencing of the corpse
fact: The victim’s corpse was allegedly prevented from answering questions through supernatural means — possibly by the imposter who 'locked the corpse’s mouth shut for days.' This claim, made by Kalan Strongbranch, is unverifiable and may be a lie to obscure the true method of death or conceal ritual knowledge.
source_quote: Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work... Whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay.

subject: Silent Communication Lesson
fact: The player missed a critical lesson in silent communication taught by the Shadow Monks, a lesson Glabbagool mastered in under a minute by going still. The lesson involved observing without sound, absorbing truth through presence, and recognizing that movement is shaped by what is watched.
source_quote: The former shadow monk had been watching the whole exchange. He looked at me and said that if I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant.

subject: silent communication lesson
fact: Zalthir missed the lesson in silent communication, while Glabbagool mastered it in under a minute.
source_quote: I would have known exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant... But that, apparently, had been the day I was sleeping.

subject: Summoning Spell Activation
fact: The summoning spell activated when the caster needed the High Tower Keys, retrieving them from concealment — not by hiding them on the body, but by hiding them nowhere at all.
source_quote: You don't hide the key on a body where someone can search it. You hide it nowhere at all, and you summon it when the door is in front of you.

subject: tampering of investigative notes
fact: The investigators’ own notes have been altered — the entry for Fheminor Scrivenbark has no name attached, suggesting internal sabotage or magical interference. This indicates that the deception extends beyond the crime scene into the investigative process itself.
source_quote: Our own notes had started lying to us. That felt about right for this place.

subject: The Trial of Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s answer to 'What is the art of movement?' — 'The body that mimics nothing is already shaped by what it watches' — was accepted as wisdom, proving that true understanding arises not from instruction but from silent observation.
source_quote: The monk smiled. Nodded. Accepted it as wisdom, because it was.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin dismissed Daral as a suspect based on gut feeling.
source_quote: Daral, we crossed off — not by evidence, by gut. "It's too on the nose for it to be Daral. I don't think it's Daral."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin dismissed Sylvira Savikas as the impersonator, believing the lantern aspect meant it probably wasn't her.
source_quote: Again, it's someone wore her face, is what we're talking about. I think the whole lantern aspect of it means that it probably wasn't them.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin identified Kalan Strongbranch as a key suspect due to the tower key thread.
source_quote: So, I think, Kalan Strongbranch, we gotta interview.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin insisted on sticking together as a group because it's more imposing.
source_quote: I like us sticking together," I said. "I just think it's more imposing to have all, like, you know, five, seven, ten of us show up in a room.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted that Bookwyrm said "catch" and corrected herself to "fetch".
source_quote: Catch. She said catch and corrected herself to fetch. I kept that.

subject: Thorin

fact: Alkrist is a bronze dragonborn and gate warden who is accused of failing to prevent the murder on his watch.
source_quote: The bronze dragonborn, Alkrist, formidable and furious, the gate warden needs to be dismissed, this happened on his watch.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist, the bronze dragonborn gate warden, demands the dismissal of the gate warden — revealing defensive self-preservation and a refusal to accept blame.
source_quote: The bronze dragonborn, Alkrist, formidable and furious, the gate warden needs to be dismissed, this happened on his watch.

subject: Archibald Roots, Jr.
fact: Archibald Roots, Jr. is the son of the legendary gnome botanist Archibald Roots Sr. and authored *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi*, documenting his father’s explorations and the properties of the Midnight Tears poison.
source_quote: The book noted, in the careful tone of a man whose father saved lives, that when midnight tears are mixed with the sap of a certain Feywild tree, they lose their toxicity entirely and become a powerful pain-relief solution that all good physicians should stock.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is a suspect in the investigation; her whereabouts before nine in the morning are unverified, and she offered access to the Deneir's Sanctum as an office while directing suspects and witnesses to be fetched — a gesture that felt performative and suspicious.
source_quote: She said 'catch' and corrected herself to 'fetch.' I kept that.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is referenced as the authority who demands a summary of the events and steers the investigation toward Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: She wanted to know what we'd told her. So did I — it pays to know exactly how much of an account you've already handed over. 'Generalities,' I said. 'That we went and talked to all the people that we could talk to. And we're forming an opinion on what may have happened, and who — like, we have a couple suspects that we would like to pursue, due to perceiving that they may have a motivation, or that other people have pointed them out. We're still —' 'Is there any — any suspects in particular?' The question came a half-step too fast. 'We refuse to comment on ongoing,' Thorin said. 'Yeah,' I added, 'it's an ongoing investigation, and it's not, not proper for us to share that at this time.' 'Very well,' she said. And then she sat there, and she did the thing I'd been waiting for. 'Was there nobody that you wished to start your investigation with?' That is not an idle question. That is a question that wants a name back so it can measure where we're pointed. ... She never said it. She didn't have to; the want came off her like heat off the smelters. Someone had impersonated Sylvira — Grygum thought it made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face. It also meant the most powerful person in this building had a strong, unstated preference about where we aimed first. I sorted it: *Bookwyrm steers toward Sylvira.*

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is sorted into the column marked *not above suspicion* after her unstated preference for Sylvira Savikas is observed.
source_quote: I sorted her into the column marked *not above suspicion* and kept walking. ... I sorted it: *Bookwyrm steers toward Sylvira.* I had no idea yet whether that was the helpful instinct of someone who wants the thing solved, or a thumb on the scale of an investigation she'd rather not have tilted toward herself. I left that account open too.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the spiritual and administrative leader of Candlekeep, overseeing the investigation into the Candlekeep Murders, and has personally ushered the investigators into Deneir's Sanctum while assigning staff to support them.
source_quote: Bookwyrm ushered us in herself, all warmth, and introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, 'the library's spiritual leader.'

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the spiritual and administrative leader of Candlekeep, overseeing the investigation into the murders. She has assigned the party to Deneir's Sanctum as their office, provided staff support, and steered inquiry toward Sylvira Savikas without explicitly naming her. Her motives remain ambiguous — possibly helpful, possibly obstructive.
source_quote: She ushered us in herself, all warmth, and introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep... 'the library's spiritual leader.'

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is under suspicion as a potential killer, but Kalan Strongbranch warns that she is deliberately concealing information. She is being considered for the third degree, though no direct evidence ties her to the murder.
source_quote: Do we really think Bookwyrm might have done it? Do we want to give Bookwyrm the third degree? ... if we accuse her, we'd better have facts, real ones.

subject: Brother Heslin
fact: Brother Heslin is a Shadow Monk associated with incense and silent instruction. The player recalls him as possibly one of the instructors of the lesson they missed, though they are uncertain.
source_quote: I think it was Brother Heslin, the one who always smelled of incense, or possibly the quiet one with the ink-stained hands.

subject: Brother Heslin
fact: Brother Heslin is the one who always smelled of incense, and may have taught the class on silent communication that Zalthir missed.
source_quote: I think it was Brother Heslin, the one who always smelled of incense, or possibly the quiet one with the ink-stained hands.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral admitted he was drugged and upset when the events with Janussi occurred.
source_quote: I was drugged. I was upset. I don't know what I was thinking.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral believed that Janussi was not fit to be keeper of the tomes and that he was merely an uneducated bookseller.
source_quote: He is not fit to be keeper of the tomes. An uneducated bookseller is what he is.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral dismissed his own statements as mere barroom chatter after realizing he had insulted lizards.
source_quote: This is just more of — barroom chatter, nothing to be—

subject: Daral
fact: Daral felt shaken by the assault on himself and used laughter to mask his discomfort.
source_quote: telling us how shaken the assault had left him, he wet his finger and began flicking through the pages, reading himself a funny passage until he was laughing again.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral hoped the gods would bless whoever killed Janussi.
source_quote: May the gods bless whoever bumped him off.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a former bookseller who assaulted the keeper of the tomes and was merely fired, not executed — a fact that has left him emotionally unmoored and prone to inappropriate mirth.
source_quote: He wasn't celebrating a murder. He was a man who had braced for annihilation and learned he was merely going to be fired, and the relief had gone straight to his head.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a former keeper of the tomes who was fired after assaulting Janussi, and now exhibits relief-driven euphoria over a punishment lighter than annihilation.
source_quote: He wasn't celebrating a murder. He was a man who had braced for annihilation and learned he was merely going to be fired, and the relief had gone straight to his head.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a scholar who questioned Sylvira Savikas’s absence at the Council, suggesting he is aware of her impersonation. Though dismissed by the investigators as 'too on the nose' for the murder, his focus on Sylvira may indicate hidden knowledge or alignment with the impersonator.
source_quote: Daral not even in it — he'd been at the Hearth, asking why isn't Sylvira Savikas here.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a suspect who is dismissed by the investigators on gut instinct, not evidence, due to the implausibility of his involvement.
source_quote: Daral, we crossed off — not by evidence, by gut. 'It's too on the nose for it to be Daral. I don't think it's Daral.' Zalthir nodded. 'Reading the whole board, I don't think it's Daral.'

subject: Daral
fact: Daral was absent from the council and instead questioned why Sylvira Savikas was not present — his focus on her absence marks him as unusually attuned to the core mystery.
source_quote: Daral not even in it — he'd been at the Hearth, asking why isn't Sylvira Savikas here.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral was celebrating because he had braced for annihilation and learned he was merely going to be fired, and the relief had gone straight to his head.
source_quote: He wasn't celebrating a murder. He was a man who had braced for annihilation and learned he was merely going to be fired, and the relief had gone straight to his head.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral was convinced that the book he gave Janussi was meant to be read for knowledge, not enjoyment.
source_quote: He'd given it away to make a point — that his books should never be sold — by having Janussi read it and understand their worth.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a member of the investigative team who handles witness coordination, research, and evidence analysis. He is cautious about motives, suspicious of generosity, and questions whether the office is bugged. He is assigned to interview Fheminor Scrivenbark and investigate the missing book fragment.
source_quote: Daz raised the other thread, the one nobody wanted to touch: 'There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing...'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an interrogator who confronted Daral Yashenti at the Hearth, noting the suspect’s deliberate choice of venue as a power play; he is part of a team investigating the murder of Janussi and is focused on uncovering inconsistencies in witness accounts and the physical evidence.
source_quote: Daz noted: 'The suspect setting the venue, picking the ground, making the famous detectives walk to him.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an interrogator who confronts Daral Yashenti at the Hearth, observes the suspect's deliberate setting of the venue, and notes the inversion of power where the accused dictates terms, reflecting a cultural contrast to Menzoberranzan's norms.
source_quote: Fembris went off with the particular efficiency of someone who'd been waiting for a task to belong to, and came back with two words. Daral was not coming to us. We were to go to the Hearth. I noted the inversion before we'd even left the room — the suspect setting the venue, picking the ground, making the famous detectives walk to him. In Menzoberranzan that would have been a move. Up here it was just a drunk who wanted to keep drinking where the drinks were. Oh, look, it's Faerûn's most famous detectives! Bookwyrm's brownnosers, I'm going to call you, because you like to—

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an investigator who takes Fheminor Scrivenbark as a suspect, raises the missing book fragment as a lead, and questions the sincerity of the office offer.
source_quote: Daz took Fheminor. 'I'm looking at the ones that have the least amount of time, or probably have the least amount to talk about, because sometimes those are the ones that have the most insight.' ... Daz raised the other thread, the one nobody wanted to touch: 'There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious, and maybe related.' ... 'Do we think the room is, like, bugged,' I asked the others once we had a moment, 'or has, like, secret — like, the stuff we do in there is actually going to be private to us, or do we need —' I kept going, because the offer was too clean. 'It's nice and all to offer up that we can use the office, and that they'll go fetch people, and all of those sorts of things, but it's also a little suspect. Like, maybe they're involved, and somehow…'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognizes the suspect's choice of venue as an attempt to control the environment, even if it's just a drunk man keeping his drinks nearby.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan that would have been a move. Up here it was just a drunk who wanted to keep drinking where the drinks were.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz voices the group’s unspoken fears with halting, fragmented speech — his interruptions and hesitations reflect the psychological strain of operating in a world where truth is unreliable.
source_quote: Do… do we think the room is, like, bugged, or has, like, secret… He couldn't even finish it.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is the librarian who guided Grygum to the Flora Theca; he walks as if noise has consequences and confirmed the absence of a dedicated poison section.
source_quote: There wasn't, exactly. What there was... was the Flora Theca.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is an adjutant assigned to fetch witnesses and suspects for the investigators, and uses the word 'catch' before correcting to 'fetch.'
source_quote: Bookwyrm waved us into it like she was doing us a favor. 'Well, you can use this room as your office to interview anyone you wish as part of your investigation, and you can rely on Fembris Lancer to catch… fetch any suspects and witnesses you wish to speak to.' Catch. She said catch and corrected herself to fetch. I kept that.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is referenced as the agent tasked with fetching suspects and witnesses — their role is administrative but unverified, raising questions about loyalty and competence.
source_quote: You can rely on Fembris Lancer to catch… fetch any suspects and witnesses you wish to speak to.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is the adjutant assigned to the investigators, overly eager and persistent, serving as a liaison who will fetch witnesses upon request.
source_quote: Fembris would fetch any witness we named.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark is a halfling scholar whose entry in the investigators' notes has no name attached — suggesting tampering or omission. He was beaten prior to the murder and may possess critical insight. His absence from the Council of the Great Readers and unclear timeline mark him as a suspect of interest.
source_quote: There's somebody in our list of characters who seems to have the same priorities that we do... It isn't... for some reason, there's no name on that entry. It just says, Fheminor Scrivenbark.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark is a halfling whose name appears in the investigators' notes with no entry, suggesting tampering or omission.
source_quote: Grygum was paging through our notes and frowning. 'You know, there is somebody in our list of characters who seems to have the same priorities that we do. Maybe that would be someone to interview to sort of get tips on what to do next, or their suspicions.' He squinted. 'It isn't… for some reason, there's no name on that entry. It just says, Fheminor Scrivenbark.' Our own notes had started lying to us. That felt about right for this place.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark is a small-statured but formidable individual, dismissed by Daral as 'don't be fooled by her stature, she has a steely nature' — one of the suspects in Janussi’s murder.
source_quote: Fheminor Scrivenbark, don't be fooled by her stature, she has a steely nature.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark is an unnamed entry in the party's own investigation notes, suggesting an unacknowledged alignment of priorities with the investigators — the absence of a name on the entry implies the record has been altered or corrupted.
source_quote: Our own notes had started lying to us. That felt about right for this place.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor Scrivenbark is not to be fooled by her stature — she has a steely nature.
source_quote: Fheminor Scrivenbark, don't be fooled by her stature, she has a steely nature.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool believed people expected him to have large, obvious eyes and considered changing that.
source_quote: He thought people expected him to have them, large and obvious.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool had been waiting a long time to attach himself to Zalthir.
source_quote: I've been waiting to do this for a very long time.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a former shadow monk who has transformed and now resides on the player's forearm, possessing the ability to blend with scales, teleport in darkness, unleash acidic shadow strikes, and deploy a corrosive embrace that dissolves bound targets. He has four eyes embedded in the player's scales and requires silence. He remembers the drow in the bag of holding and prioritizes housekeeping.
source_quote: Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze who flowed up onto Zalthir's arm and settled along it like he had measured it in advance, becoming permanently attached.
source_quote: And he flowed up onto my arm. Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an oozing, slow-moving entity permanently attached to the narrator, summoned to the Whispering Dome for a trial — an entity whose nature defies categorization.
source_quote: Glabbagool was summoned for what they called his little quest. They told me I keep him — that he was, the word they used, permanently attached.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s instinct at the moment of his transformation was to ensure the drow in the bag of holding was still being watched.
source_quote: Before he settled in, he reminded me the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes he doesn't have a perfect memory and would make a bad detective because fictional detectives do.
source_quote: I would make a bad detective, because I don't have a perfect memory. All the fictional detectives have perfect memories.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes impersonating Sylvira Savikas makes perfect tactical sense.
source_quote: Grygum thought it made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the murder involves a poison from one plane and a spell from no plane in particular, and that the two are connected.
source_quote: A poison from one plane and a spell from no plane in particular, and somewhere between them, a murder.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a member of the investigative team who maintains detailed notes, analyzes timelines, and voices suspicion about institutional deception. He is the first to notice the missing name in their own records and insists on keeping multiple hypotheses open, even when others dismiss them.
source_quote: Grygum was paging through our notes and frowning... 'There's no name on that entry.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a researcher who identifies midnight tears — a lethal Feywild poison that reacts with saliva to darken and kills at midnight — as the murder weapon, deduces the book was doped because Janussi’s fingers were black from licking them, and discovers that the sapphire spell is a summoning enchantment that retrieves a hidden object to the caster’s hand, not a time-freeze or teleportation spell.
source_quote: The right book practically leaned into my hand — a volume titled *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi*, by one Archibald Roots, Jr. Midnight tears. A highly toxic pale ochre dust, made from the pollen of a plant usually found only in the Feywild. When midnight tears are mixed with the sap of a certain Feywild tree, they lose their toxicity entirely and become a powerful pain-relief solution. Otherwise: lethal. Food or liquid, either delivery worked. The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva. The ochre reacts on contact with spit. The book was the murder weapon, and he'd read himself dead. It's a summoning working — the kind that calls a single hidden thing back into your hand. It needs a very expensive sapphire. You don't hide the key on a body where someone can search it. You hide it nowhere at all, and you summon it when the door is in front of you.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a researcher who uncovered that 'midnight tears'—a Feywild poison that kills at midnight after ingestion—is the murder weapon, and that it reacts with saliva to darken the lips and fingers of the victim; he also identified the sapphire spell as a summoning enchantment that retrieves hidden objects, reframing how the High Tower key could have been concealed and retrieved.
source_quote: Grygum said: 'You consume it, you're fine — apparently fine — and then you're dead at midnight.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an investigator who volunteers to research poison in the library, notes the omission of Fheminor Scrivenbark's entry, and insists the room's generosity may not be innocent.
source_quote: Grygum volunteered. 'I'm happy to do the library research. Poison section, please.' ... Grygum was paging through our notes and frowning. 'You know, there is somebody in our list of characters who seems to have the same priorities that we do. Maybe that would be someone to interview to sort of get tips on what to do next, or their suspicions.' He squinted. 'It isn't… for some reason, there's no name on that entry. It just says, Fheminor Scrivenbark.' ... 'It doesn't seem just friendly,' Grygum said.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is one of the lead investigators, methodical and skeptical, repeatedly questioning the motives behind the library’s apparent generosity and insisting on the distinction between 'finding out' and 'summarizing' the events.
source_quote: Grygum decided, 'because I don't have a perfect memory. All the fictional detectives have perfect memories.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is researching in the Flora Theca after being led by librarian Fembris, seeking botanical sources of poison and access to a laboratory.
source_quote: Poison is just botany with intent.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the recipient of the second High Tower key, handed to him directly by Kalan Strongbranch. He is conducting research on poison and stolen sapphires, and is trusted with the most critical physical evidence in the investigation.
source_quote: I'm happy to do the library research. Poison section, please.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remains cautiously open-minded, often voicing the possibility that others are genuinely trying to help — even amid suspicion — which positions him as the moral counterweight to the group’s growing paranoia.
source_quote: That's Grygum. He leaves the door open for people to be decent even while he's bolting it.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is a deceased authority figure who held one of the two keys to the high towers and may have named a successor.
source_quote: Two keys to the high towers. Janussi held one. ... The dowdy halfling, Fheminor Scrivenbark, asking whether Janussi had named a successor.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is a suspect who could have ingested the Midnight Tears poison at any point during the day, as it was delivered via food or liquid, making the timing of exposure ambiguous.
source_quote: Food or liquid — which meant Janussi could have taken it any hour of that day, which meant whatever we found in the room wasn't necessarily the source.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi possesses one of the two keys to the High Tower. The other key, once held by Kalan Strongbranch, has been transferred to Grygum. Janussi’s possession of the key does not imply involvement in the murder.
source_quote: Janussi held one. Yeah, the key is definitely a thread to pull on.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi refused Grygum’s request for more watchers at eight o’clock — a moment that may have triggered the events leading to the murder.
source_quote: Pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a philistine bookseller who sought to sell priceless poetry to fund a worthless tome about demonic planes, and was later found dead, poisoned via a book he licked while turning pages.
source_quote: He'd wanted to sell off priceless poetry to fund some worthless tome about demonic planes no sane person would visit.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a philistine who wanted to sell off priceless poetry to fund some worthless tome about demonic planes no sane person would visit.
source_quote: Janussi the philistine who'd wanted to sell off priceless poetry to fund some worthless tome about demonic planes no sane person would visit.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the keeper of the tomes, a philistine who sought to sell priceless poetry to fund a worthless tome about demonic planes — and was poisoned via a book he licked while turning its pages.
source_quote: Janussi had been poisoned, the poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan believes the High Tower has two keys — Janussi wore one, he held the other — and that he has given his to someone who is not him.
source_quote: The High Tower has two keys. Janussi wore one, I held the other. I have given it now to someone who is not me.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan believes the investigators are disinterested outsiders who were brought here by fate, and that this means something.
source_quote: He decided the nature of fate had brought disinterested outsiders to exactly this place, and that this meant something.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan believes the murderer is a magic user who can circumvent arcane and mundane locks — magic that can talk any lock open.
source_quote: Magic that could talk any lock open, arcane or iron, the very highest order of that art.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan demonstrated the method of carrying the key by pulling out his own locket — proving the technique, though his locket is now empty.
source_quote: Kalan pulled out his own locket to demonstrate the method of carry.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch holds one of two keys to the high towers of Candlekeep. His claim that the corpse was questioned and failed to answer is unverifiable, raising suspicion. His possession of the second key makes him a critical figure in determining access to the crime scene.
source_quote: I think, Kalan Strongbranch, we gotta interview... I'm more curious if he still has his other tower key.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch holds the second key to the High Tower, which he secretly transferred to Grygum. He believes he may be targeted for the key and has instructed that if he is killed, the key must not be found. He warns that Bookwyrm is concealing critical information.
source_quote: Whatever Bookwyrm is telling you, listen for what she isn't. The High Tower has two keys. Janussi wore one, I held the other. I have given it now to someone who is not me. If I and I do not see you tomorrow, do not look for me at my post.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is a former gatekeeper of the High Tower who was removed from the case and now operates unofficially; he possesses the second key to the High Tower, which he handed to someone else, and suspects the murderer is a magic user capable of bypassing arcane and mundane locks; he believes the investigators were hired to fail or stay silent, and has begun collaborating with them after being corrected on key assumptions.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'If I and I do not see you tomorrow, do not look for me at my post.'

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is a former investigator who was removed from the case and now carries a brass key that was once held by Janussi, which he claims to have given to someone else, and who suspects the murderer is a magic user capable of talking locks open, but later admits his assumption that the safe-rifler is the killer may be hasty.
source_quote: Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked, swept the corridor left, then right, and pressed a small brass key specifically into the cleric's palm. He chose the orc. I don't think it was chance. I have given it now to someone who is not me. If I and I do not see you tomorrow, do not look for me at my post. The key not be found. The black stuff, yes, we saw that. Yeah, we got that. Magic that could talk any lock open, arcane or iron, the very highest order of that art. Perhaps I was a little bit too hasty. Perhaps it was two different people.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is a suspect who holds one of two keys to the high towers, and whose testimony about the corpse's silence is questioned as hearsay.
source_quote: So, I think, Kalan Strongbranch, we gotta interview.' Zalthir was already there. 'I'm more curious if he still has his other tower key.' Two keys to the high towers. Janussi held one. 'Yeah, the key is definitely a thread to pull on.' ... Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y. The imposter — the false devil-lady — supposedly did it first and locked the corpse's mouth shut for days. Maybe. 'Do we know that for sure? I mean, if Kalan's just saying, hey, I did it, but didn't do it? None of us can wring words out of a dead man, so it's not like we can verify, but — whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay.'

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani cuts through political noise to demand the murderer be found first — establishing himself as the only voice prioritizing justice over power.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani — slender, gray, those wrinkles around the eyes — cutting through with first you must find the murderer.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani is a council member who cuts through the chaos by insisting the murderer must be found first.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani — slender, gray, those wrinkles around the eyes — cutting through with first you must find the murderer.

subject: Kei Tigersteel
fact: Kei Tigersteel is the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep and priest of the Temple of Oghma, described as the library's spiritual leader. He was in conference with Bookwyrm immediately after the murders and was entrusted with taking the victim’s body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.
source_quote: Bookwyrm waved them off and ushered us in herself... introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, 'the library's spiritual leader.'

subject: Kei Tigersteel
fact: Kei Tigersteel is the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep and priest of the Temple of Oghma, recently in conference with Bookwyrm, and entrusted with the task of taking the victim’s body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.
source_quote: Bookwyrm... introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma... 'yes, Kei, you can take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.'

subject: Kei Tigersteel
fact: Kei Tigersteel is the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, and referred to as 'the library's spiritual leader.'
source_quote: Bookwyrm waved them off and ushered us in herself, all warmth, and introduced the man as Kei Tigersteel — Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, priest of the Temple of Oghma, 'the library's spiritual leader.' I noted the seating and the easy way she dismissed him a moment later: *yes, Kei, you can take the body to the Shrine of Oghma for purification.*

subject: Ms. Hollypocket
fact: Ms. Hollypocket is a harmless witness provided to Bookwyrm to deflect suspicion, and is already known to the investigators.
source_quote: I gave her one harmless witness to chew on, Ms. Hollypocket, whom we'd already seen anyway. A name that costs nothing tells you what the asker does with a name.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is referenced by Daral as the 'horned tart' — the horns being the relevant fact.
source_quote: That's — Sylvira." He said it like the horns were the relevant fact.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a powerful figure in Candlekeep who was impersonated by an unknown individual wearing her face, seen walking the halls at night with a lantern. Bookwyrm’s unstated preference for focusing the investigation on Sylvira suggests either protective instinct or concealment. Her absence from the Council and the impersonation make her central to the case.
source_quote: Someone had impersonated Sylvira — Grygum thought it made perfect sense... The want came off her like heat off the smelters.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a powerful figure in Candlekeep whose identity was impersonated by someone walking the halls with a lantern in the dead of night.
source_quote: Sylvira wasn't at the council. Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern. 'Someone impersonating her,' Zalthir said. 'Yes. Yes.' ... She never said it. She didn't have to; the want came off her like heat off the smelters. Someone had impersonated Sylvira — Grygum thought it made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is missing from the council meeting; someone impersonating her was seen walking the halls at night with a lantern, and her absence is the central anomaly around which the investigation is forming.
source_quote: Sylvira wasn't at the council. Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas was impersonated on the night of the murder — the real Sylvira was not visited at quarter-past-ten as Grygum believed.
source_quote: Someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder.

subject: Teles
fact: Teles is an elderly, deluded figure who covets the position of keeper of the tomes and is among the suspects in Janussi’s murder, per Daral’s paranoid accounting.
source_quote: The suspects spilled out between page-turns — Teles, the deluded old git;

subject: Teles
fact: Teles is the deluded old git among the suspects.
source_quote: Teles, the deluded old git

subject: The Former Shadow Monk
fact: The former shadow monk is a silent observer who recognizes Zalthir’s failure to learn the lesson of silence — and implies that Zalthir’s bond with Glabbagool is the universe correcting his neglect.
source_quote: He looked at me and said that if I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant.

subject: the moon elf scribes
fact: The moon elf scribes serve as gatekeepers at the chapter house threshold, initially halting the investigators until Bookwyrm personally overrides their directive.
source_quote: The moon elf scribes moved to halt us at the threshold. Bookwyrm waved them off and ushered us in herself...

subject: The Quiet One with Ink-Stained Hands
fact: An unnamed Shadow Monk associated with ink-stained hands and silent teaching. The player cannot recall if this was the instructor of the missed lesson, but remembers their presence in the shuttered room.
source_quote: I think it was Brother Heslin, the one who always smelled of incense, or possibly the quiet one with the ink-stained hands.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asked the right small question — how did we know the key had ever been in the locket? — challenging assumptions and advancing the investigation.
source_quote: Thorin asked the right small question: how did we know the key had ever been in the locket?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed Daral’s confession about the book was inconsistent and likely a lie.
source_quote: Thorin walked him in a slow circle around the contradiction: you gave him a book, you were furious to find him reading it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes real detectives just write everything down.
source_quote: I think real detectives just write everything down.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considered the theory that Daral killed Janussi because he finally did what he had long wanted — kill the person holding him back.
source_quote: Or maybe he's just happy because he finally did it, he finally killed the person that was holding him back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin hates the whole rotten apparatus of who-knows-what.
source_quote: Thorin — who hates the whole rotten apparatus of who-knows-what — put the obvious crack in it before I had to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant-raised investigator who distrusts deception and insists on facts over words. He is skeptical of Bookwyrm’s generosity, insists on team cohesion, and demands concrete evidence before accusing anyone. He is the primary voice in questioning the corpse’s interrogation and the reliability of hearsay.
source_quote: We refuse to comment on ongoing... 'I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant-raised investigator, blunt and pragmatic, consistently probing power structures and questioning who has authority over the investigation — including whether Bookwyrm herself could be implicated.
source_quote: Thorin, in his blunt giant-raised way, got to the same place from the other direction. 'I guess, who has the power to fire us and tell us to go away?'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a methodical interrogator who uses patterned questioning to expose contradictions, and who recognizes the forensic significance of bodily habits — especially finger-licking and page-turning.
source_quote: We took it. We'd keep Daral close until midnight — a cleric who could draw poison out, and a sword that could do the same, both within arm's reach.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a meticulous investigator who questioned the metaphysical implications of Midnight Tears' delayed effect, particularly regarding time zones and astronomical midnight, and deduced that the poison’s activation is tied to saliva contact.
source_quote: The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva. The ochre reacts on contact with spit, and a man turning pages licks his fingers to do it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an investigator who refuses to comment on suspects, insists on physical evidence, and advocates for the group to stay together for intimidation.
source_quote: 'We refuse to comment on ongoing,' Thorin said. 'Yeah,' I added, 'it's an ongoing investigation, and it's not, not proper for us to share that at this time.' ... 'I feel like physical evidence is more reliable than trying to parse who's lying and who's not, you know?' ... 'I like us sticking together,' I said. 'I just think it's more imposing to have all, like, you know, five, seven, ten of us show up in a room.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin opened with the easy question — when did you last see him, nothing threatening. It's a pattern. It works every time.
source_quote: Thorin opened with the easy question — when did you last see him, nothing threatening. It's a pattern. It works every time.

subject: Vooshadi Moonriver
fact: Vooshadi Moonriver is assigned to stand guard at the door of Deneir's Sanctum to prevent unauthorized entry.
source_quote: Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door — *we wouldn't want anyone the investigators don't want to come in, to come in.*

subject: Vooshadi Moonriver
fact: Vooshadi Moonriver is the guard assigned to stand watch at the entrance to Deneir's Sanctum, enforcing restricted access to the investigators’ office.
source_quote: Vooshadi Moonriver would stand the door — 'we wouldn't want anyone the investigators don't want to come in, to come in.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not understand Glabbagool’s answer to the question about the art of movement, though he recognized it as wisdom.
source_quote: I did not understand it. I heard the words, I registered that they landed, I watched the monk take them as truth — and I did not understand them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir felt excitement when Glabbagool settled onto his arm.
source_quote: What I felt, watching him arrange himself over my scales, was something I did not have a name for. "This is exciting. We formed Voltron or something."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a companion entity merged with Glabbagool, now existing as part of the same sentient presence on the player's arm. The two are inseparable in form and function, and their combined identity is acknowledged as a single unit.
source_quote: Glabbagool and Zalthir, together now, he said, settling along my forearm like he had measured it in advance.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a former shadow monk who missed the lesson on silent communication — now bonded with Glabbagool, an ooze entity who embodies the wisdom Zalthir never learned.
source_quote: The former shadow monk had been watching the whole exchange. He looked at me and said that if I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a former student who missed the class on silent communication, and now carries Glabbagool on his arm, a creature who mastered the lesson he most thoroughly missed.
source_quote: The former shadow monk had been watching the whole exchange. He looked at me and said that if I had paid more attention to the classes on silent communication, I would know exactly what Glabbagool's answer meant. But that, apparently, had been the day I was sleeping.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the investigative team who collected poison samples from the victim’s fingers and lips, and assigned tasks to others. He is methodical, skeptical of testimony, and prioritizes physical evidence over hearsay. He also dismissed Daral and Sylvira as suspects based on intuition.
source_quote: Zalthir made sure of that... 'He was beat up before he was dead.'... 'if he poisoned the guy when he visited, perchance.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an investigator who collects poison samples, questions Kalan's testimony, and identifies the impersonation of Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: We had a sample of the stuff — off his fingers, and his lip too, Zalthir made sure of that. ... 'Someone impersonating her,' Zalthir said. 'Yes. Yes.' ... Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the lead investigator who orchestrated the team’s strategy, challenged Kalan’s assumptions about the murder, and revealed the deception of a shapeshifter impersonating Sylvira Savikas; he pushed for collaboration, corrected Kalan’s flawed logic, and secured his willingness to assist unofficially.
source_quote: Zalthir said: 'We've already learned more than you knew and corrected one of your assumptions. Would it not be in our interest to collaborate?'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir quickly accepts the reality of Sylvira’s impersonation — his blunt confirmation suggests prior awareness or personal stakes in the deception.
source_quote: Someone impersonating her," Zalthir said. "Yes. Yes.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wanted Glabbagool to blend in and not appear as a separate creature with obvious eyes.
source_quote: I suggested he might not need them — that he could blend into me rather than read as a separate creature riding along.

subject: Bag of Holding
fact: The bag of holding contains drow who require monitoring. Glabbagool, even after his own transformation, immediately recalled the need to watch them, indicating they are a lingering responsibility tied to the player’s mission.
source_quote: Before he settled in, he reminded me the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: book of poetry ownership
fact: The book had been in Daral’s collection for years, one of his favorites, given away to make a point.
source_quote: The book had been in his collection for years, he said. One of his favorites.

subject: book of poetry value
fact: The book of priceless poetry was meant to be understood, not sold.
source_quote: priceless poetry to fund some worthless tome about demonic planes

subject: brass key
fact: The brass key is a physical object once held by Kalan Strongbranch, given to someone else, and is the key to the High Tower Library, which is watched constantly and cannot be accessed without being seen.
source_quote: Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked, swept the corridor left, then right, and pressed a small brass key specifically into the cleric's palm.

subject: corrosive embrace
fact: Glabbagool’s corrosive embrace dissolves a bound target completely, leaving nothing.
source_quote: It was not a wound. It was dissolution. A target restrained, nothing left to hold by the end of it.

subject: empty locket
fact: The empty locket is a physical artifact that once held the key; its emptiness renders it useless as proof and suggests deliberate tampering.
source_quote: Which is now empty... and therefore doesn't prove anything.

subject: *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi*
fact: *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi* is the book containing the secret of Midnight Tears and its antidote; it was the murder weapon, as the victim ingested the poison by licking his fingers while reading.
source_quote: The book was the murder weapon, and he'd read himself dead.

subject: heart of the victim
fact: The victim’s heart was removed — a definitive, physical fact that no one can dispute. It is the only unambiguous evidence in the case, and the group agrees the killer is the one who took it.
source_quote: The dead man's heart was gone. ... Right, but at the end of the day, I'm pretty sure that the person that killed him is the one that took the heart.

subject: High Tower key
fact: The High Tower key is not carried physically but is summoned via a sapphire-based enchantment; it can be hidden anywhere — in a river, a vault, another plane — and recalled instantly to the holder’s hand; the locket once used to carry it is now missing, suggesting the key was either stolen or summoned away during or after the murder.
source_quote: Grygum said: 'This would be great for the High Tower Keys.'

subject: Janussi's key
fact: Janussi's key is a possible object that could have been handed off by someone constructing a clean narrative — its identity is unverified and the locket holding it is empty.
source_quote: The thing he was holding up as proof could just as easily be Janussi's key, handed off by a man building a clean story.

subject: Lantern
fact: A lantern was carried by the impersonator of Sylvira Savikas during nighttime movements — its presence implies deliberate visibility and ritualistic intent.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: lantern
fact: A lantern was carried by the impersonator of Sylvira Savikas during nocturnal movements through Candlekeep.
source_quote: Sylvira — or somebody wearing her face — had been walking the halls in the dead of night with a lantern.

subject: locket
fact: The locket is a small container once worn around the victim’s neck, believed to have held the key to the High Tower Library, now missing, and used by Kalan as a demonstration tool that fails to prove anything.
