source_quote: The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone. So why would the killer go through the safe at all? Kalan pulled out his own locket to demonstrate the method of carry. Which is now empty, and therefore doesn't prove anything.

subject: locket
fact: The locket was the traditional vessel for carrying the second High Tower key, worn around the neck; it is now empty and missing, making it impossible to verify whether it once held Janussi’s key or if it was planted as part of a cover story; its absence implies either theft or deliberate removal to obscure the key’s true method of concealment.
source_quote: Zalthir said: 'The locket was missing. The key was in the missing locket.'

subject: locket
fact: The locket, once containing the key, was worn around the keeper’s neck and is now missing — its absence undermines the assumption that the safe was breached by the same person who stole the key.
source_quote: The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone.

subject: loket-key mechanism
fact: The key was carried inside a locket worn around the victim’s neck, now missing.
source_quote: The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone.

subject: midnight tears
fact: Midnight tears is a pale ochre Feywild poison that kills at midnight after ingestion, reacts with saliva to darken surfaces, and was likely administered via a book Janussi licked his fingers to turn.
source_quote: Midnight tears. A highly toxic pale ochre dust, made from the pollen of a plant usually found only in the Feywild. The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva. The ochre reacts on contact with spit.

subject: midnight tears
fact: Midnight tears is a pale ochre dust derived from Feywild pollen; it is lethal when ingested but becomes a pain reliever when mixed with a specific Feywild sap; it reacts with saliva to turn black, leaving telltale stains on lips and fingers; it activates precisely at midnight, regardless of time zones or daylight savings, due to magical calibration.
source_quote: Grygum said: 'The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva.'

subject: midnight tears poison
fact: Midnight tears is a pale ochre dust from Feywild pollen that kills at midnight when ingested, and darkens upon contact with saliva.
source_quote: Midnight tears. A highly toxic pale ochre dust, made from the pollen of a plant usually found only in the Feywild. [...] The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva.

subject: missing book fragment
fact: A fragment of a book is missing — possibly a volume of forbidden knowledge, possibly centuries old. Its absence is suspicious and may be linked to the murder, the impersonation, or the silencing of the corpse. Daz has been assigned to investigate its provenance.
source_quote: There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing... that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious.

subject: missing book fragment
fact: A missing fragment of a book, potentially centuries old, is suspected to be related to the murders and is being investigated by Daz.
source_quote: Daz raised the other thread, the one nobody wanted to touch: 'There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious, and maybe related.'

subject: poison on the victim's fingers
fact: Poison was found on the victim’s fingers and lips, but its origin and intent remain unverified. It may have been planted, self-administered, or irrelevant — a red herring disguised as evidence.
source_quote: A smear of poison on a dead man's fingers doesn't have a motive. ... But, you know, maybe that's from watching too much CSI, what do I know?

subject: poison sample
fact: A poison sample is being sought in the Flora Theca — though none is cataloged separately, Grygum believes botany holds the answer.
source_quote: I asked if there was a poison section... Poison is just botany with intent.

subject: poison sample
fact: A poison sample was collected from the victim's fingers and lip, and is being analyzed for identification.
source_quote: We had a sample of the stuff — off his fingers, and his lip too, Zalthir made sure of that. Grygum volunteered. 'I'm happy to do the library research. Poison section, please.'

subject: poison sample
fact: A sample of the poison used to kill Janussi was collected from his fingers and lips. It is being analyzed for origin and composition. The poison’s rarity and method of delivery suggest a knowledgeable killer, possibly connected to the library’s forbidden archives.
source_quote: Zalthir made sure of that... 'I'm happy to do the library research. Poison section, please.'

subject: research notes
fact: Grygum’s research notes in the Flora Theca are being compiled to identify possible poisons — though no dedicated poison section exists.
source_quote: I asked if there was a poison section. There wasn't, exactly.

subject: Sapphire (in summoning spell)
fact: A sapphire of very high value is required as a component for a summoning spell that retrieves a hidden object and brings it into the caster’s hand, regardless of location.
source_quote: It needs a very expensive sapphire.

subject: sapphire summoning spell
fact: The sapphire summoning spell is a high-level arcane working that retrieves a hidden object — such as a key — directly into the caster’s hand, regardless of its location, and requires a very expensive sapphire as a focus.
source_quote: It's a summoning working — the kind that calls a single hidden thing back into your hand. It needs a very expensive sapphire. You don't hide the key on a body where someone can search it. You hide it nowhere at all, and you summon it when the door is in front of you.

subject: second High Tower key
fact: The second key to the High Tower, previously held by Kalan Strongbranch, was secretly given to Grygum. It is the only physical object that can grant lawful access to the tower’s inner sanctum, and its transfer is the central act of the secret meeting.
source_quote: I have given it now to someone who is not me.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: stolen sapphires
fact: The stolen sapphires were expensive but not rare, and their value alone was deemed insufficient to motivate murder. Grygum has cataloged them alongside poison in his research, treating them as circumstantial.
source_quote: Grygum asked whether the stolen sapphires were worth killing for — expensive, not rare, was the answer — and tucked it into his library list alongside the poison.

subject: the bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding still contained drow who needed watching, and Glabbagool's instinct at the moment of his own transformation was housekeeping.
source_quote: Before he settled in, he reminded me the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: The Bag of Holding (with Drow)
fact: A container holding captured drow, which Glabbagool insists must be monitored — a detail that reveals his priorities: even in transformation, he remains a caretaker of responsibility.
source_quote: Before he settled in, he reminded me the drow in the bag of holding still needed watching.

subject: the body
fact: The body of the victim has been removed from the crime scene and transported to the Shrine of Oghma for purification, suggesting ritual significance to the death.
source_quote: The body went to be purified.

subject: the book
fact: The book had been in Daral's collection for years, one of his favorites, which he gave away to make a point — that his books should never be sold — by having Janussi read it and understand their worth.
source_quote: The book had been in his collection for years, he said. One of his favorites. He'd given it away to make a point — that his books should never be sold — by having Janussi read it and understand their worth.

subject: the book (Daral's favorite)
fact: This book was Daral's personal favorite, given to Janussi as a symbolic gesture to teach its worth — later found stained with poison and handled repeatedly by Daral's own fingers.
source_quote: The book had been in his collection for years, he said. One of his favorites. He'd given it away to make a point... and then he'd been enraged to find Janussi reading it.

subject: The Book (formerly Daral's favorite)
fact: A treasured volume given by Daral to Janussi as a symbolic gesture — later found saturated with poison, licked and turned by Janussi, and now the key forensic artifact in his murder.
source_quote: He produced the book to prove it. And then, telling us how shaken the assault had left him, he wet his finger and began flicking through the pages, reading himself a funny passage until he was laughing again.

subject: the poisoned book
fact: The poison was carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.
source_quote: Janussi had been poisoned, the poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: the scales
fact: Glabbagool's four eyes blinked up from Zalthir's own scales, and Zalthir suggested they blend into him rather than read as a separate creature.
source_quote: Four, as it turned out, blinking up from my own scales. I suggested he might not need them — that he could blend into me rather than read as a separate creature riding along.

subject: the sword and cleric (evidence tools)
fact: A sword and a cleric capable of drawing poison are kept within arm's reach of Daral — tools of both protection and execution, should he die before midnight.
source_quote: We'd keep Daral close until midnight — a cleric who could draw poison out, and a sword that could do the same, both within arm's reach.

subject: tower key
fact: A tower key is one of two keys to the high towers, held by Janussi and Kalan Strongbranch, and is a critical physical clue in the investigation.
source_quote: Two keys to the high towers. Janussi held one. 'Yeah, the key is definitely a thread to pull on.'

subject: tower key
fact: There are two keys to the high towers of Candlekeep — one held by Janussi, the other by Kalan Strongbranch. The keys are critical to determining access to the murder scene. The fact that one key remains unaccounted for raises suspicion that the murderer had lawful access.
source_quote: Two keys to the high towers. Janussi held one... 'the key is definitely a thread to pull on.'

subject: sapphire summoning spell
fact: A rare summoning spell requiring an expensive sapphire that recalls a hidden object to the caster’s hand, regardless of location.
source_quote: It's a summoning spell [...] needs a very expensive sapphire [...] you can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.

subject: truth-piercing magic
fact: Kalan possesses a magic capable of detecting lies or revealing hidden truths, usable if suspicion arises.
source_quote: He could sort it out? "Of course I could."

subject: Bahamut's Observation
fact: It is unclear whether Bahamut was watching the investigator’s deductions — a metaphysical thread left open as a reflection on divine oversight in matters of justice and arcane murder.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching me work it out. I took notes either way.

subject: Blending vs. Visibility
fact: The player suggests Glabbagool should blend into their scales rather than appear as a separate creature. Glabbagool considers this, acknowledging that others expect him to be obvious — raising questions about identity, perception, and the burden of expectation.
source_quote: I suggested he might not need them — that he could blend into me rather than read as a separate creature riding along. 'Right, she doesn't need the eyes, right?' He thought people expected him to have them, large and obvious.

subject: book as weapon
fact: The book is not merely evidence — it is the delivery mechanism for poison, transforming the sacred object of knowledge into a tool of murder.
source_quote: The poison was carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages.

subject: bookkeeping as motive
fact: The narrative frames violence not as anger, but as cold, logical bookkeeping — a lesson made legible through slaughter, a theme that mirrors the poisoning as a calculated act of retribution.
source_quote: It isn't anger. It's bookkeeping. You failed, and the account closes.

subject: Bookwyrm's possible involvement
fact: Bookwyrm’s behavior — steering the investigation toward Sylvira, offering overly convenient resources, and her unverified whereabouts before the murder — suggests she may be the killer, an accomplice, or trying to cover for someone else. The team has left this hypothesis open, with no conclusive evidence yet.
source_quote: I sorted it: Bookwyrm steers toward Sylvira... I had no idea yet whether that was the helpful instinct... or a thumb on the scale of an investigation she'd rather not have tilted toward herself.

subject: Bookwyrm's possible involvement
fact: There is an unresolved suspicion that Bookwyrm may be connected to the murders, as the investigators openly debate whether her generosity is genuine or a cover, and whether she herself could be the perpetrator.
source_quote: I'm just saying, like, if Bookwyrm ended up doing it, which I don't think she did, but… then. This could get awkward.

subject: Bookwyrm's unstated preference
fact: Bookwyrm steers toward Sylvira Savikas, though she never says it aloud.
source_quote: What she did was want Sylvira Savikas. She never said it. She didn't have to; the want came off her like heat off the smelters.

subject: collaboration proposal
fact: Grygum proposed an offline, private collaboration — syncing up with the team to examine all evidence together — signaling a shift from isolation to cooperation.
source_quote: Offline chat, private work streams, a meeting to examine everything one by one...

subject: Daz's Insight
fact: Daz’s internal voice provided a critical interpretation of the summoning spell as a teleportation-to-hand mechanism, bridging practical application with theoretical understanding.
source_quote: I heard Daz say it in my head — 'Oh, wait a second, this is like a way to teleport it into my hand later kind of thing.'

subject: false devil-lady imposter
fact: An imposter posing as a devil-lady is suspected of having tampered with the corpse’s ability to answer questions, but this claim is hearsay and unverified. Kalan’s assertion that 'it didn't work because of Y' is the only source, and may be a lie.
source_quote: Kalan said they'd put the question to the corpse, and that it didn't work. And that didn't work because of Y. ... whether the corpse was ever truly made to answer is hearsay.

subject: falsified notes and institutional deception
fact: The alteration of the investigators’ own records — particularly the erased name of Fheminor Scrivenbark — indicates that deception is institutionalized within Candlekeep. This suggests the library’s leadership may be actively obstructing the investigation or concealing its own complicity.
source_quote: Our own notes had started lying to us. That felt about right for this place.

subject: fate of the missing key
fact: The key’s current location is unknown; it was in the locket, which is now missing — its disappearance undermines all prior assumptions about the crime’s mechanics.
source_quote: The key was in the missing locket. None of it forced his conclusion.

subject: finger-licking pattern
fact: The recurring act of licking fingers to turn pages is the key behavioral clue — the poisoner must have handled the book with a wet finger, and Daral was observed doing exactly that before and after the murder.
source_quote: I watched the finger go to the mouth and back to the paper. I was fairly sure I knew what I was watching.

subject: Gardening Research
fact: The player’s excuse for missing critical lessons — 'Too much gardening research' — is a recurring motif that symbolizes their distraction from deeper spiritual or magical disciplines in favor of mundane, safe pursuits.
source_quote: 'Too much gardening research.'

subject: Glabbagool's True Nature
fact: Glabbagool’s final statement — 'I've been waiting to do this for a very long time' — and his immediate mastery of stillness suggest he is not merely a transformed monk but possibly an ancient or dormant entity awakening. His ease with the lesson hints at prior existence beyond the Shadow Monks' teachings.
source_quote: Glabbagool came out of his stillness and said, 'I've been waiting to do this for a very long time.'

subject: Grygum's dismissal
fact: Grygum was fired from the case — he believes it was to protect someone, and he now suspects the dismissal itself was part of the cover-up.
source_quote: He had been wanted off the case... reminded us, twice.

subject: identity of the imposter
fact: The identity of the person who impersonated Sylvira Savikas remains unknown. The imposter’s knowledge of her appearance, movements, and access to the library at night suggests either an insider or someone with magical means. This thread may lead to the killer, the missing book, or the corruption of the corpse.
source_quote: Someone impersonating her... the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face.

subject: identity of the murderer
fact: The murderer is a magic user capable of bypassing both arcane and mundane locks; they removed Janussi’s heart post-mortem to prevent resurrection; they poisoned him via a book laced with midnight tears; they stole the locket containing the second key; they impersonated Sylvira Savikas; and they may be part of the Great Readers — but the true identity remains hidden, and the investigation is still open.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'The murderer was a magic user who could circumvent arcane and mundane locks.'

subject: impending additional murders
fact: Grygum warns that more murders are likely, implying that the killer is active and the library’s response is inadequate. The pressure to conclude the investigation quickly suggests that higher powers wish to bury the truth before more bodies appear.
source_quote: Grygum put it plainest: 'There'll be more murders.'

subject: Kalan's belief
fact: Kalan believes the investigators were hired to bungle the case or remain silent if they found the truth.
source_quote: You're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case, or else be silent if you do happen upon the right scent. You don't matter. You're outsiders.

subject: Kalan's disappearance
fact: Kalan Strongbranch has warned that if he does not appear tomorrow, he will be dead — and the key must not be found. His disappearance is anticipated, and his fate is now a central unresolved thread.
source_quote: If I and I do not see you tomorrow, do not look for me at my post.

subject: Kalan's suspicion
fact: Kalan suspects one of the Great Readers is the murderer, and that Bookwyrm is protecting them or was convinced to fire him to protect themselves.
source_quote: I believe one of the Great Readers is the murderer, and that either Bookwyrm was protecting them or someone had convinced her to fire him to protect themselves.

subject: missing book part
fact: A missing portion of a book is referenced as a possible clue, but its relevance is vague and speculative. It is mentioned as a thread no one wanted to touch, suggesting it may be a deliberate misdirection.
source_quote: There's a missing part of, like, a book that should not be missing… that could have happened a hundred years ago or something, but… seems suspicious, and maybe related.

subject: missing heart
fact: The victim’s heart is the central thread of the investigation — the only unambiguous, physical evidence that identifies the killer. Everyone else’s claims, suspicions, and theories are noise compared to this fact.
source_quote: The heart is a fact.

subject: Missing Silent Communication Lesson
fact: The player missed the core lesson on silent communication and stillness taught by the Shadow Monks — a lesson Glabbagool mastered instantly. This absence remains unresolved, and the player is aware they were likely sleeping during it, symbolizing a deeper pattern of disengagement.
source_quote: But that, apparently, had been the day I was sleeping. 'Too much gardening research.'

subject: motive inversion
fact: Daral’s rage over Janussi reading the book he gave him suggests he did not want the book read — contradicting his stated intent — implying the gift was a ruse to ensure its contamination.
source_quote: He'd given it away to make a point — that his books should never be sold — by having Janussi read it and understand their worth. And then he'd been enraged to find Janussi reading it.

subject: Origin of the Poison Delivery
fact: The exact method by which the poison was introduced to the book — whether by the killer directly or via an intermediary — remains unconfirmed, though the saliva-triggered mechanism implies intimate access.
source_quote: So somebody doped up the book.

subject: purpose of the team's employment
fact: The team’s employment is suspected to be a setup — they were hired to bungle the case or remain silent if they uncover the truth.
source_quote: You're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case, or else be silent if you do happen upon the right scent.

subject: surveillance in Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The investigators suspect that their office may be bugged or monitored, given the excessive hospitality and the library’s insistence on controlling access — raising the question of whether their work is truly private.
source_quote: Do we think the room is, like, bugged... or does the stuff we do in there is actually going to be private to us?

subject: sync-up collaboration
fact: The thread of collaboration between the party and Kalan forms a private, offline workstream to merge findings, marking a turning point where official barriers are ignored in favor of truth-seeking.
source_quote: He proposed it in the most extraordinary terms — offline chat, private work streams, a meeting to examine everything one by one, the four of us and him, five streams, merge it all in a few hours. 'I hope you actually used the word sync up,' I said. 'That makes me happy.'

subject: The Eyes on the Arm
fact: Glabbagool’s four eyes embedded in the player’s scales raise questions about identity, perception, and concealment. The player wonders if they can be hidden to blend in — suggesting an ongoing tension between visibility and integration.
source_quote: Four, as it turned out, blinking up from my own scales. 'Well, good! So I just admire him now.'

subject: The fake Sylvira
fact: Someone impersonated Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder, and this was unknown to Kalan until revealed.
source_quote: Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder? 'No. That is new information.'

subject: the fate of the second key
fact: The second High Tower key was removed from the locket and may have been summoned away using the sapphire spell; its current location is unknown; it may be in the hands of the murderer, an accomplice, or hidden in a place only the summoner can retrieve it from; its absence is the central mystery tying the murder, the impersonation, and the magical artifacts together.
source_quote: Zalthir said: 'The key was in the missing locket.'

subject: The Finger on the Page
fact: The act of wetting a finger and turning pages is not innocent — it is the vector of poison, the signature of the killer, and the unconscious habit of the innocent — making Daral both suspect and victim.
source_quote: I watched the finger go to the mouth and back to the paper. I was fairly sure I knew what I was watching.

subject: The identity of Bookwyrm's employer
fact: It is unclear who hired Bookwyrm, or why they would fire Kalan to protect someone — or if they even did.
source_quote: Someone had convinced her to fire him to protect themselves.

subject: the identity of the first person to interview
fact: Bookwyrm’s abrupt question — 'Was there nobody that you wished to start your investigation with?' — implies she expected a specific target to be named first, hinting at prior knowledge or agenda.
source_quote: Was there nobody that you wished to start your investigation with?

subject: the innocent poisoner
fact: The true poisoner is likely the one who licked the book’s pages — but the dead man, Janussi, was the only one observed doing so — suggesting the real culprit is the one who framed him by ensuring the poison was on the book he’d handle.
source_quote: The dead poisoner is the innocent one.

subject: The locket key
fact: The locket key is missing, and its presence around the victim’s neck was never proven — only assumed.
source_quote: The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone. So why would the killer go through the safe at all?

subject: the nature of the investigation's mandate
fact: The investigators are uncertain whether their role is to uncover the truth or merely to provide a summary for Bookwyrm — a tension that underlies their entire approach and their reluctance to share details.
source_quote: I thought we were asked to find out what — well, I guess summarizing the events is pretty much the same as finding out who did it from one.

subject: The origin of the poison
fact: Midnight tears are rare and only accessible to those with Feywild connections — but the source of the poison remains untraced.
source_quote: A poison from another plane narrows your suspect list considerably.

subject: The Paradox of the Book
fact: Daral gave Janussi the book to teach its worth — then raged when Janussi read it — revealing a contradiction: he wanted the book to be understood, but not enjoyed — a theological dissonance that mirrors his own moral confusion.
source_quote: He'd given it away to make a point — that his books should never be sold — by having Janussi read it and understand their worth. And then he'd been enraged to find Janussi reading it.

subject: the purpose of hiring the investigators
fact: The investigators were likely hired not to solve the case, but to bungle it or remain silent if they uncovered the truth; this suggests a powerful entity — possibly within Bookwyrm’s circle or the Great Readers — orchestrated the murder and the investigation to mislead or obscure the real culprits.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'You're only being employed so you're likely to bungle the case, or else be silent if you do happen upon the right scent.'

subject: The sapphire summoning spell
fact: The sapphire summoning spell could be used to hide the High Tower key — but it is unknown who possessed the spell or the sapphire.
source_quote: This would be great for the High Tower Keys.

subject: The second key
fact: The second key — Kalan’s — was given to someone who is not him, but that person’s identity remains unknown.
source_quote: I have given it now to someone who is not me.

subject: The shapeshifter
fact: It is suspected that a shapeshifter was involved — but no evidence confirms who or how.
source_quote: Keep in mind there are people who can change their form. Shapeshift. Whatever you want to call it.

subject: The Silence That Wasn't Learned
fact: Zalthir attended the class on silent communication but remembers nothing — while Glabbagool, an ooze, mastered it in a minute by doing nothing — revealing that wisdom is not taught, but absorbed.
source_quote: The student on my arm had mastered the one lesson I most thoroughly missed, and he had done it in under a minute, by going still.

subject: The Silent Lesson of Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s answer — 'The body that mimics nothing is already shaped by what it watches' — reveals a profound, untaught truth about absorption and identity that Zalthir failed to learn in class, despite having been present.
source_quote: Glabbagool held it like it was the easiest thing he had ever been asked to do.

subject: The true motive
fact: The motive behind the murder — and the framing of the investigators — remains unknown.
source_quote: Whoever set this up, he said — naming him to the wrong people, perhaps — would be very disappointed in him.

subject: The true murderer
fact: The murderer may be two different people — one who poisoned the book, and one who rifled the safe — but this remains unconfirmed.
source_quote: Perhaps it was two different people.

subject: The True Nature of Daral's Laughter
fact: Daral’s laughter is not mere absurdity — it is the psychological residue of surviving a punishment system that should have killed him, and his mirth is the symptom of cognitive dissonance between expectation and reality.
source_quote: He deflected to the others — they wanted the top job, every one of them, Bookwyrm and Teles and A'lai and Fheminor, round and round.

subject: Time Zone Ambiguity
fact: The activation of Midnight Tears at midnight raises unresolved questions about whether 'midnight' refers to local time, astronomical midnight, or a magical standard, with no consensus among investigators.
source_quote: How do they account for daylight savings time? Did you ever… an astronomical midnight?

subject: true identity of the murderer
fact: The true identity of the murderer remains unresolved; multiple suspects and false assumptions have been introduced, including shapeshifters, magic users, and the Great Readers.
source_quote: I don't know. What I thought — but now that you bring it up, perhaps I was a little bit too hasty.

subject: truth vs. hearsay
fact: The entire investigation is built on conflicting narratives — rumors, claims, and interpretations. The only truth is the missing heart. Everything else is people talking, and the group has resolved to rely only on physical facts.
source_quote: Everything else is people talking. The heart is a fact. ... I'd rather that, honestly. One conversation, one truth, no committee.

subject: Voltron Analogy
fact: The player’s comparison of Glabbagool’s integration to 'Voltron or something' reveals a disconnect between their understanding and the depth of the Shadow Monk philosophy. The analogy reflects a pop-culture lens applied to a sacred, ancient discipline.
source_quote: 'This is exciting. We formed Voltron or something.'

subject: Who Is Behind the Impersonation Scheme?
fact: The impersonation of Sylvira Savikas is part of a broader scheme — the timing, access, and precision suggest coordination with someone inside the investigation or authority structure.
source_quote: It made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face.

subject: Who is the Real Sylvira Savikas?
fact: The identity of Sylvira Savikas is in question — whether she is missing, dead, or was never who she claimed to be — and this uncertainty is the central unresolved thread driving the investigation.
source_quote: Someone impersonating her," Zalthir said. "Yes. Yes.

subject: Who Ordered the Impersonation?
fact: The impersonation of Sylvira Savikas was too precise and timely to be random — someone with access to her identity, schedule, and influence orchestrated it, but their motive and identity remain hidden.
source_quote: It made perfect sense, and tactically it did, the impersonated woman might know who would wear her face.

subject: Who Really Killed Janussi?
fact: The true killer may be Daral — who licked the book’s pages and poisoned himself — or someone else who used his habit as a cover — making the act of reading a crime and the innocent the only one who could have done it.
source_quote: The dead poisoner is the innocent one.

subject: who set this up?
fact: The mastermind behind the setup is unknown — they may have named Grygum to the wrong people, leading to his dismissal and the murder.
source_quote: Whoever set this up, he said — naming him to the wrong people, perhaps — would be very disappointed in him.

subject: Why Are Records Being Altered?
fact: The investigators' own notes have begun omitting or obscuring names — suggesting magical tampering, internal betrayal, or systemic corruption within their investigation apparatus.
source_quote: Our own notes had started lying to us.

subject: Why Is the Investigation Being Rushed?
fact: The investigators are told they will only be allowed to pursue a limited number of threads — suggesting external forces are controlling the pace of justice to prevent exposure.
source_quote: Apparently they don't. Apparently things keep happening while you're standing around thinking. Grygum put it plainest: 'There'll be more murders.'

subject: Worn vs. Carried Objects
fact: There is an unresolved magical distinction between objects worn (e.g., on a lanyard) and objects carried, impacting whether the summoning spell can retrieve items worn but not held.
source_quote: Whether a thing worn counts as a thing carried. 'I would think so. I'd think that you're carrying anything that you're wearing.' It doesn't, as it turned out.

subject: Zalthir's Disappointment
fact: Zalthir expected a time-freezing spell but received a summoning spell instead, revealing a gap in assumptions about magical intent and highlighting the unpredictability of arcane knowledge.
source_quote: Zalthir had been expecting a working that freezes a thing in stopped time, and seemed almost disappointed.

subject: Zalthir's silence class
fact: Zalthir missed the class on silent communication and does not remember what was taught.
source_quote: I remember the light through the shutters. I do not remember the lesson.

subject: Zalthir's sleeping days
fact: Zalthir suspects he was sleeping during many important lessons, including the one Glabbagool mastered.
source_quote: There are, by now, a great many days I was sleeping. The student on my arm had mastered the one lesson I most thoroughly missed, and he had done it in under a minute, by going still.
